status: read-only reconciliation of the user-selected wildcard default

baseline.interpretation_required: A wildcard zero is the fallback for a relation signature absent from the effective whitelist. A more-specific named signature may allow its own source, target, direction, and source-side cardinality; it does not grant any other endpoint, direction, inverse, or override a named zero. Without this specificity rule, the wildcard is an absolute contradiction with every positive signature.

common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.signature: Primary Node -> Primary Node only; HAS_NARROWER is derived inverse.
common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.property_effect: No Property grant. declare-node.md:29-32 requires HAS_NARROWER zero when the Node is a Property.

common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.signature: Property -> immediate Node bearer, source cardinality exactly one; HAS_PROPERTY is derived inverse.
common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.property_effect: The common exception covers all Property Declarations through inheritance. No local duplication across 60 Properties is warranted.

common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.signature: Node instance -> Primary Node; HAS_INSTANCE is derived inverse; Property has HAS_INSTANCE zero.
common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.why_required: Node//** includes instances. If INSTANCE_OF is not a named exception or excluded from wildcard scope, the new baseline forbids the existing common instantiation signature.

common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.signature: Only the explicit classification signatures already used by common/Primary constraints, including Node -> Independence for Primary Node/Property classification.
common_exceptions_supported_by_live_mode.why_required: `>| Independence` is a written classification relation in the live Node common constraint. The wildcard otherwise forbids the classification that distinguishes Property from Primary Node. This is not blanket permission for arbitrary axes.

non_graph_value_binding.existing_semantics: CFEL `p: literal` and `p: [format]{:n}` define an admitted value domain; HAS_VALUE binds an admitted literal to a Property instance.
non_graph_value_binding.reconciliation: Neither colon nor HAS_VALUE is a Node-to-Node graph Relation, so neither is an exception to `((*))`. A typed reference value remains a value binding and does not create an endpoint edge.

local_relation_constraints.rule: After the common fallback and exceptions resolve, each active Primary subject may add only its own outgoing signatures; inverse degree stays in the counterpart Declaration.
examples: Event Record -> Actor HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR is owned by Event Record, not Event Record.Relations.HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR Property.
Containment, RUN, and other Primary-specific relations require their own declared endpoint signatures; common relation-definition mention alone is not permission.
local_relation_constraints.no_local_property_duplication: A Property path, relation-like child name, prose mention, or `[Actor//]`/other typed value format does not justify a local graph-edge grant.

guardrails: A named positive signature never ignores its endpoint selectors, direction, or source-side cardinality.
A named zero remains effective even when another relation is allowed.
Derived inverse views are not independently authored permissions.
Unresolved effective whitelist remains deny, as required by the inheritance/whitelist Rule.

one_user_question.question: Does `ALLOWED VALUE` mean the existing non-graph colon/HAS_VALUE value-domain binding, or do you intend a new graph Relation named ALLOWED_VALUE?
one_user_question.why_it_matters: The first needs no wildcard exception and preserves typed references as values; the second needs a new Relation Definition, endpoints, cardinality, inverse policy, and changes the value-versus-edge boundary.
